slot.brief: Given limiting molar conductivities of two strong electrolytes, compute Λ°m of a weak electrolyte (e.g. CH3COOH from NaCl, HCl, CH3COONa).

stem: Given $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})=426.0$, $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})=126.4$ and $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})=91.0$, all in $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, find $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})$.

verdicts.working: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426.0 + 91.0 − 126.4 = 390.6 S cm² mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})$\n$=426.0+91.0-126.4=390.6\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Independent check: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426.0 + 91.0 − 126.4 = 390.6 S cm² mol⁻¹.
solution:
By Kohlrausch’s law, the limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid is
$$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})$$
$=426.0+91.0-126.4=390.6\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.
